item.title: Structure, Coordination, and Power in Agrifood Markets
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on examining the structural characteristics, coordination mechanisms, and power relationships that shape contemporary agrifood markets. The call seeks research that investigates how different organizational arrangements, market concentration, and power asymmetries influence the functioning of agricultural and food systems.

Appel publié par Food Policy. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Market structure in agrifood systems
  • Coordination mechanisms in food chains
  • Power dynamics in agricultural markets
  • Market concentration and consolidation
  • Supply chain organization
  • Buyer power and supplier relationships
  • Vertical integration in agriculture
  • Market governance structures

Timeline

  • June 15, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Resilient, Inclusive and Digital Supply Chains for Africa's Sustainable Development
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how supply chains can advance sustainable development across Africa by integrating resilience, inclusivity, and digital innovation. The focus encompasses strategies to manage disruptions in volatile environments, approaches to include SMEs and local communities in value chains, and the application of artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies to enhance efficiency and transparency.

The issue welcomes rigorous, peer-reviewed contributions from academics, practitioners, and policymakers addressing digital transformation, risk management, sustainability, and sector-specific applications in healthcare and agribusiness. The goal is to develop equitable, robust supply chain systems that support Africa's sustainable development objectives.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Building resilient and risk-responsive supply chains
  • Inclusive supply chain models for local economic participation
  • Sustainable and green supply chain practices
  • Artificial intelligence and digital transformation in African supply chains
  • Sector-specific innovations in critical industries

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • January 29, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) for Tariffs and Supply Chains: Pathways to Resilient Economic Planning
item.content:encoded:

The collection seeks research that demonstrates how MCDA frameworks can inform more resilient approaches to economic planning in increasingly complex and interconnected global markets.

item.title: International Business in a Reconfiguring Southeast Asia
item.content:encoded:
S. Tamer Cavusgil, Georgia State University

Southeast Asia is a critical yet underrepresented region in international business research, despite hosting the world's fifth-largest economic bloc and attracting record foreign investment. The region's distinctive characteristics—diverse political systems, family capitalism networks, state-linked enterprises, and rapid digital development—challenge existing international business theory but remain largely absent from leading journals.

This focused issue invites contributions that treat Southeast Asian phenomena as theoretically generative rather than merely illustrative, particularly welcoming scholars based in the region. The collection addresses four themes: internationalization of Southeast Asian multinationals, supply chain reconfiguration, geopolitical hedging strategies amid great-power competition, and indigenous theorizing drawing on Southeast Asian intellectual traditions to advance broader international business literature.

Appel publié par Management International Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Internationalization of Southeast Asian multinationals
  • Springboard and asset-augmentation strategies of ASEAN MNEs
  • Digital-native champions and platform architecture
  • State-linked enterprises internationalization
  • Supply chain reconfiguration and global value chain integration
  • Maritime connectivity and port competitiveness
  • Supply chain resilience and logistics
  • Cross-border trade and geopolitical hedging
  • Non-market strategy under strategic ambiguity
  • Middle-power firms and neutral coordination hubs
  • Indigenous theorizing and Southeast Asian intellectual traditions
  • Multi-language qualitative research methods
  • Postcolonial perspectives on knowledge production
  • Ethnographic and historical-archival fieldwork

Timeline

  • March 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Alternative Proteins for Sustainable and Ethical Food Systems: Consumer, Production, and Supply-Chain Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
The global food system is undergoing profound transformation driven by growing concerns about climate change, biodiversity loss, animal welfare, public health, and the long-term sustainability of livestock-based production models. Against this backdrop, alternative proteins, including cultured meat, plant-based meat analogues, insect-based products and novel dairy substitutes, have emerged as promising pathways for addressing environmental pressures while meeting evolving consumer expectations for ethical, healthy and sustainable diets. Although consumer research on these products has expanded rapidly, a comprehensive understanding of how alternative proteins reshape the broader agrifood system remains limited. Existing studies often address consumption, production, regulation, and socio-cultural dynamics in isolation, leaving significant knowledge gaps regarding value-chain restructuring, producer adoption, economic feasibility, and governance.

Appel publié par British Food Journal. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumer acceptance, preferences, and willingness to pay for alternative meats and dairy products
  • Farm-level decision-making and economic feasibility of adopting alternative-protein production systems
  • Sustainability, environmental and life-cycle assessments of alternative protein supply chains
  • Regulatory frameworks, certification, labelling, and standards for emerging protein products
  • Cultural, ethical, and societal narratives shaping acceptance and legitimacy
  • Communication, trust-building, and transparency strategies across the supply chain

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions
